plan.name: 10-Week Strength & Conditioning (Power Clean / Bench)
plan.description: Hybrid strength-and-running plan for a 45-year-old with managed tennis elbow and goose-foot knee. This 10-week sample uses Monday bench strength, Wednesday clean quality, Friday squat strength plus positional squat backoff work, Tuesday run development, Thursday recovery running plus structural support, and Sunday long easy aerobic work.
plan.author: Power Clean / Bench Plan

exercises.notes: 2-3 min general heat before pressing.
exercises.coachingNotes: Easy pace only. Raise temperature and get the shoulders moving without accumulating fatigue.

exercises.notes: 10 each direction. Run 1-2 rounds through the early Monday warm-up work.
exercises.coachingNotes: Slow circles only. This is joint prep for the elbow and wrist, not a stretch challenge.

exercises.notes: One crisp set before bench activation work.
exercises.coachingNotes: Move through full scapular protraction and retraction without bending the elbows.

exercises.notes: Pick the option that gives you clean scapular depression without elbow irritation.
exercises.coachingNotes: Use the smallest range that lets the shoulder blades move freely and pain-free.

exercises.notes: Weeks 5-8 can skip this if shoulders feel good and you want the extra pull-apart set noted below.
exercises.coachingNotes: Keep ribs down and let the scapula rotate upward instead of shrugging.

exercises.notes: Part of the bench activation block. In Weeks 5-8 you can add a second set if shoulders feel good.
exercises.coachingNotes: Finish with the shoulder blades moving together, not the low back extending.

exercises.notes: 10 per side.
exercises.coachingNotes: Keep the elbow pinned and rotate only as far as you can control without the shoulder rolling forward.

exercises.notes: Brace hard and keep the torso quiet.
exercises.coachingNotes: This is anti-rotation trunk prep for the press, not a speed drill.

exercises.notes: 2-3x3. Weeks 1-4 use the shallowest crisp variation; Weeks 9-10 can trim to 1-2 crisp reps if needed. Use the built-in alternatives when elbow tolerance dictates.
Compression primer. Weeks 9-10 can trim to one brief hold.
exercises.coachingNotes: Locked elbows, shoulders depressed, ribs tucked. Treat this as position rehearsal for the later L-sit work.

exercises.notes: 3-4 min easy jog at roughly 6:50-7:30/km. On Phase 2 Tuesdays add 2-3 relaxed strides before the mobility work.
exercises.coachingNotes: This is only to transition into the run smoothly. Resist turning the jog into the session.

exercises.notes: Hold the rig upright and let the leg swing freely without forcing range.
exercises.coachingNotes: Stay tall and let the hip open naturally rather than chasing extra height.

exercises.notes: Use the frontal plane swing to open the hips after Monday and Wednesday lifting.
exercises.coachingNotes: Control the torso and let the adductors lengthen at the edge of the swing.

exercises.notes: Step forward, bring the elbow toward the floor, then rotate open without rushing.
exercises.coachingNotes: Move through the sequence slowly enough that the hips and thoracic spine actually open.

exercises.notes: 2 x 20 m. Exaggerated march with active arm drive to set rhythm before the surges.
exercises.coachingNotes: Stay tall and crisp. This is a mechanics primer, not conditioning.

exercises.notes: 1 x 20 m. Keep the shoulders relaxed and the posture tall.
exercises.coachingNotes: Think quick contacts and upright rhythm, not sprinting.

exercises.notes: 3 seconds down on every rep. Keep this in even when the Achilles feels calm.
exercises.coachingNotes: Use the full heel drop under control and stop before the calf burns.

exercises.notes: 10 passes. Thoracic extension is usually the limiter for a clean front rack.
exercises.coachingNotes: Spend time on the stiff segments instead of rushing through the passes.

exercises.exerciseName: Lat and Shoulder Distraction at Rig
exercises.notes: 30 seconds per side with a band or by leaning away from the rig with the elbow extended.
exercises.coachingNotes: Open the lat without letting the ribs flare or the shoulder jam forward.

exercises.notes: Fingers back on the floor. Non-negotiable before cleans when the rack is sensitive.
exercises.coachingNotes: Take the stretch only to the point that the wrist opens without numbing the hand.

exercises.notes: Use heel support if needed. Rotate slowly from the deep squat without losing foot pressure.
exercises.coachingNotes: Open the thoracic spine from the bottom position rather than turning it into a fast mobility flow.

exercises.notes: Drive the knee over the pinky toe and spend more time on the stiffer side.
exercises.coachingNotes: Keep the heel heavy while the ankle moves forward.

exercises.notes: Slow and deliberate. No re-bend. Use it to feel the bar path into the rack.
exercises.coachingNotes: Keep the movement vertical and finish the elbows through before the bar gets heavy.

exercises.notes: Focus on the receiving position and front rack before you try to move it fast.
exercises.coachingNotes: Receive in the same stance and rack shape you want for the work sets.

exercises.notes: CNS primer only. Land softly. If you use acceleration sprints instead, run 2 x 15 m at roughly 80%.
exercises.coachingNotes: Stop well before fatigue and keep every landing quiet.

exercises.notes: 3-4 build-up sets from roughly 50% to 65% to 80% and then the opening work weight. If the receiving position still feels off, take one more set around 70% before opening work.
exercises.coachingNotes: Each build-up set should feel crisper than the last. Do not rush the transition from empty bar to working weight.

exercises.notes: 2-3 min before the jog starts. Lower the threshold for this day and keep it restorative.
exercises.coachingNotes: Treat the walk as permission to keep Thursday easy rather than as a performance warm-up.

exercises.notes: Floor-based external and internal rotation opening before the jog.
exercises.coachingNotes: Stay low effort and let the hips settle instead of forcing end range.

exercises.notes: 10 each direction per side to restore ankle range after Wednesday cleans.
exercises.coachingNotes: Move the joint through full circles without making it a stretch challenge.

exercises.notes: 3-4 min easy walk. Do not start the long-run timer until you are already at easy run pace.
exercises.coachingNotes: Build into the run gradually so the first minutes stay genuinely easy.

exercises.notes: 8 per leg before the longest run of the week.
exercises.coachingNotes: Let the hip loosen naturally instead of forcing more swing height.

exercises.notes: 8 each direction per side. Slow, weight-bearing hip circles before the run starts.
exercises.coachingNotes: Keep the circles controlled and use them to restore range, not to fatigue the hips.

exercises.notes: Post-clean compression work. Keep the legs straight, the toes up, and stop before the hip flexors feel heavy or the front rack gets sticky.
Wednesday tracked compression slot. Phase 1 uses tucked progressions, Phase 2 one-leg or straddle, and Phase 3 uses full L-sit work only if the elbows stay locked and the hold stays crisp.
3 min easy. This is only to raise temperature before the squat day.
exercises.coachingNotes: Keep the effort low and let the hips loosen after Thursday's lighter session.

exercises.notes: 10 passes. Upper-back extension limits both the squat shape and the clean rack.
exercises.coachingNotes: Pause on the tightest segments instead of rolling quickly through the set.

exercises.notes: 45 seconds per side with the foot on the rig or wall. Friday usually has the tightest hip flexors of the week.
exercises.coachingNotes: Stay tall through the torso and keep the glute lightly active on the stretched side.

exercises.notes: 10 per side. Address the stiffer ankle first before the squat ramp begins.
exercises.coachingNotes: Drive the knee forward while keeping the heel heavy and the arch active.

exercises.notes: Light kettlebell or dumbbell. Use these to find depth, heel contact, and torso position before the programmed broad jumps.
exercises.coachingNotes: Treat each rep as patterning work and keep the descent controlled.

exercises.notes: Run the ramp as empty bar x10, 40% x5, then 60% x3. Take the clean primer after the 60% set, then add one final 75% x2 before the first work set.
exercises.coachingNotes: Treat the bar warm-up as pattern rehearsal. The clean primer stays technical and never replaces the final squat ramp set.

exercises.notes: 3-5 min easy spin
exercises.coachingNotes: Light, easy aerobic spin to flush blood through worked tissues. Cadence smooth, breathing easy. Lower body goes here too if you just hammered upper.
Same protocol as warm-up: lift with assistance, lower 3 s solo. After hard pressing the tendon prep work doubles as recovery — do not skip.

exercises.notes: 30 s/side each
exercises.coachingNotes: Hold each position 30 s per side without bouncing. Breathe into the stretch; back off if you feel pinching at end-range. Pigeon belongs only on Friday-cooldown days when the hip is warm.
Forearm vertical against a doorframe, elbow at shoulder height. Step the same-side foot through the door until you feel a stretch across the chest. 30 s each side, no shoulder shrugging.

Hold a band at chest height, arms straight, hands shoulder-width. Pull the band apart by squeezing the shoulder blades together, finishing with the band touching the chest. Slow return. Endurance work — keep it light.

exercises.notes: 8-10 min Zone 1-2 aerobic flush
exercises.coachingNotes: Sustained Zone 1-2 effort: nasal breathing should be possible. Friday cooldown — flush the legs after the heaviest day of the week.

exercises.notes: 30 s/side each
exercises.coachingNotes: Hold each position 30 s per side without bouncing. Breathe into the stretch; back off if you feel pinching at end-range. Pigeon belongs only on Friday-cooldown days when the hip is warm.
Forearm vertical against a doorframe, elbow at shoulder height. Step the same-side foot through the door until you feel a stretch across the chest. 30 s each side, no shoulder shrugging.

exercises.notes: 10 passes. Pause on stiff segments and bias the mid-back between the shoulder blades.
exercises.coachingNotes: Roll slowly enough that the thoracic spine extends segment by segment instead of the ribs flaring.

exercises.notes: Floor or rig. Isolate scapular protraction and retraction with the elbows locked.
exercises.coachingNotes: Move only through the shoulder blades and keep the ribcage quiet.

exercises.notes: Light band. Use a thumbs-up finish on the last set to bias lower trap.
exercises.coachingNotes: Pull with the upper back instead of cranking through the low back or shrugging.

exercises.notes: Press into the wall throughout and move slowly in both directions.
exercises.coachingNotes: Keep the ribs down and let the scapula rotate upward rather than shrugging.

exercises.notes: 30 seconds in each wrist position on both arms. Keep this in even when the elbow feels calm.
exercises.coachingNotes: Take the stretch only to mild tension and keep the shoulder relaxed.

exercises.notes: Pause 1 second at the chest. Check grip width and elbow path before adding load.
exercises.coachingNotes: Treat these as rehearsal reps for the first work sets rather than fatigue work.

exerciseTemplates.notes: Power Primer Rule: 2-3 rounds x 3 plyo push-ups (handles or elevated). CNS prime before bench. Sub: med-ball chest pass if elbow > 2/10. Skip if elbow > 2/10.
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Set up with hands on raised handles or a sturdy box edge so the chest never travels deeper than parallel to the elbow. Brace hard, drive the chest away from the ground explosively, and let the hands leave the surface; reset to a controlled landing each rep. Keep the elbow path tight (~30°) — if you feel any medial-elbow pinch, switch to a med-ball chest pass and skip the plyo.

exerciseTemplates.notes: Slow and controlled - immediately before first loaded Bench set
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: In a tall plank, keep arms locked. Let the chest sag between the shoulder blades, then protract hard at the top so the upper back rounds — full scapular ROM, no elbow movement. Move slowly (~2 s up, 2 s down). The goal is to wake up serratus before the bench, not to fatigue.

exerciseTemplates.notes: Straight-bar Bench (only non-neutral grip press). 2-second eccentric. Stop set if bar speed drops or positions break.
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Eyes under the bar, shoulder blades retracted and depressed, mid-foot flat. Bar lands on the lower sternum with a 2 s controlled eccentric, no bouncing; drive heels and press in a slight J-curve back over the shoulders. If bar speed visibly slows or the elbow flares, end the set — the prescription assumes crisp reps only.

exerciseTemplates.notes: Bodyweight through Week 6 unless elbows are fully calm and reps stay crisp (Ring Pull-Up Split Progression Rule). Ring variation lets wrists rotate naturally.
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Hang from rings with thumbs slightly toward each other; let the rings rotate as you pull so the wrists self-select a neutral path. Initiate with scapular depression, finish with the chest passing the ring line. 3 s controlled descent, 1 s pause at the dead hang — no kipping, no swinging. Stop the set when full ROM breaks down.

exerciseTemplates.notes: Compression-Goal Rule (Monday). Tucked progressions Phase 1; one-leg / straddle Phase 2; full L-sit work Phase 3.
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Grip parallettes with locked elbows, shoulders pressed down (away from the ears), legs squeezed straight with toes pointed. Drive the hips forward and crunch the rib cage toward the pelvis to "compress" — this, not just leg strength, is the goal. Pick the hardest variation you can hold with locked elbows for the full duration.

exerciseTemplates.notes: Monday compression upgrade. Use a small plate or ankle weights and keep every rep crisp.
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Sit tall in a hard pike with hands by the hips, knees locked, toes up. Add a small external load with ankle weights or a light plate, then lift the heels and, if possible, the hips from the floor without leaning back. Treat each rep as an active compression contraction, not a momentum swing.

exerciseTemplates.notes: Phase 1 Monday pull support. Untimed quality rows after Ring Pull-Ups; stop 2-3 reps shy of fatigue.
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Set the rings or barbell so a chest-to-rings finish takes ~1 s of pulling. Body stays a rigid plank (glutes squeezed, ribs down). Pull until the chest touches, hold a 2 s squeeze, then lower in 1 s. Rest 60-75 s between sets. This is scapular quality work after pull-ups, not a density challenge.

exerciseTemplates.notes: Phase 2 Monday pull support EMOM: 1 assisted chest-to-rings top hold per minute. Keep scapular depression clean and stop if elbows feel loaded.
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Set the rings high enough that the top position is easy to reach. Start each minute with one chest-to-rings hold, squeeze shoulder blades down and back, keep ribs tucked, then step out and rest for the remainder of the minute. This reinforces the top position without adding row volume after pull-ups.

exerciseTemplates.notes: Hook grip (elbow management). Vertical bar path, smooth pulls, no grinding. Convert to Clean Pulls if catches get sloppy or slow.
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Start from the hang at mid-thigh with hook grip and lats engaged. Initiate with a violent leg drive and hip extension; the bar travels up the body, not away. Catch in a quarter-squat with elbows whipping through high and the chest tall. Reset every rep — singles strung together, never touch-and-go.

exerciseTemplates.notes: Explosive extension ABOVE knee; finish tall. Positional/technical reinforcement.
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Same setup as the clean but without the catch. Pull off the floor with patience, accelerate hard once the bar passes the knees, finish with a tall triple extension and a vertical shrug. Keep arms straight throughout — this is a positional and CNS primer, not a row.

exerciseTemplates.notes: Variation Dose Rule: Friday clean variation is a TECHNICAL PRIMER. Fast, sharp reps only. Stop the set if turnover slows.
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Start with the bar at the hip crease, dip the knees ~10 cm, and immediately re-extend explosively. The bar barely moves before the catch — focus on a fast turnover with the elbows whipping under. Treat every rep like a max-velocity primer; if speed drops, stop the set even if the prescription is unfinished.

exerciseTemplates.notes: Hook grip. Full power clean from floor. Convert to Clean Pulls if positions break.
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Setup: bar over mid-foot, hook grip, hips slightly higher than the squat. First pull is patient and bar-path vertical; second pull explodes once the bar passes the knees. Catch in a controlled quarter-squat with vertical torso. Drop and reset between reps — quality, not density.

exerciseTemplates.notes: Box at exactly parallel (~41-43 cm). True 1-second dead stop on box, no rocking. HLM rule: load programmed below Friday Back Squat in every week (gap by phase: -5 kg Phase 1, -7.5 to -12.5 kg Phase 2, -20 kg Wk 10). 2.5-3 min rest in Wks 7-10.
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Box height set to exactly parallel. Sit back onto the box with vertical shins, dead-stop for a true 1 s with no relaxing the trunk, then drive the floor away and stand. No rocking, no bouncing. The dead stop kills the stretch reflex — that's the point.

exerciseTemplates.notes: Tripod foot, knees track over toes. 1-second pause at depth (Phases 1-2). If knees irritated, drop 5 kg from listed load.
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: High-bar position across the upper traps, elbows tucked under the bar. Brace 360°, break at hips and knees together, descend to one inch below parallel with a controlled 1 s pause. Drive the chest up and the floor away simultaneously. If the knees protest, drop 5 kg and tighten the descent tempo.

exerciseTemplates.notes: Hinge Rule: shins vertical, 3-0-1-0 tempo. Stop at deepest pain-free hamstring position. Loads ~40-55% of 155 kg DL.
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Bar starts at the hip with a soft knee bend (~15°). Push the hips straight back, keeping the bar in contact with the thigh and then the shin; descend to the deepest point you can reach without lumbar rounding. 3 s eccentric, no pause, smooth concentric. Hamstring stretch — not lower back — should be the limit.

exerciseTemplates.notes: Phase 1: 20-25 kg/hand build. Phase 2: 25-30 kg/hand. Wks 9-10: 20-25 kg/hand back-off. Upper end only when scapular control is perfect.
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Chest pinned to the pad, feet planted, dumbbells hanging straight down. Pull the elbows back and slightly out (~45°) until the handles touch the ribs; squeeze the shoulder blades together at the top, then lower under control. No torso rocking — if you need to swing, the load is too heavy.

exerciseTemplates.notes: Neutral-grip dumbbell bench, 1-second pause. Submaximal secondary press (stay 2-3 reps shy of failure).
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Lie on a flat bench with dumbbells held in a neutral grip. Keep shoulder blades set, wrists stacked over elbows, and elbows 30-45° from the torso. Lower to a comfortable pain-free depth, pause 1 s, then press smoothly without letting the bells drift apart. Stop the set 2-3 reps shy of failure — this is a secondary press for volume, not a rep test.

exerciseTemplates.notes: Medium grip, 2-second chest pause. Bench-specific without extra triceps/elbow stress. Min 2 min rest.
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Standard bench setup with a medium grip. Lower the bar to the lower sternum, pause 2 s with active tension (not collapsed on the chest), then press. The pause builds raw start strength without adding ROM stress. Min 2 min rest so the press is fresh, not fatigued.

exerciseTemplates.notes: Compression-Goal Rule (Wednesday). Active toe lift, lift hips off floor with straight legs. Quality over quantity.
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Sit tall with legs straight and toes actively pulled toward you. Press the hands into the floor next to the hips and lift the heels (and ideally the hips) off the ground while keeping the legs perfectly straight. Each rep is a small, controlled pulse — no kipping the legs up.

exerciseTemplates.notes: Best L-Sit variation, target 8-15 s. Use after Wednesday clean work for low-fatigue compression volume.
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Pick the hardest L-sit progression you can hold with locked elbows, depressed shoulders, and legs straight. Press the floor away, lift the chest, and crunch the ribs toward the pelvis. Stop the hold the moment the legs drop or the elbows bend.

exerciseTemplates.notes: Light Weighted Jefferson Curl. Smooth spinal segmentation only; replace one Friday pike set in Phase 2.
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Stand tall holding a very light load. Tuck the chin and slowly articulate one spinal segment at a time as you roll down, then reverse the motion from the pelvis up. Keep the load light enough that the rep stays smooth and restorative rather than straining.

exerciseTemplates.notes: Easy aerobic run for a conservative 5k build, RPE 5-6. Rough pace guide: 6:40-7:20/km. Warm up 5-10 min easy + dynamic mobility. Cool down 3 min easy walk or jog. Use Bike or SkiErg only if the knee is not happy with running that day.
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Conversational pace only. Given the low current run volume, finish feeling undertrained rather than accomplished. Run tall, keep cadence light, and shut it down if the calves, Achilles, or knee start to complain. If you need to run slower than 7:20/km to stay easy, do that.

exerciseTemplates.notes: Controlled Fartlek session for early 5k support, RPE 6-7. Use smooth surges and active easy jog recoveries rather than hard stop-start reps. Rough guide: easy jog around 5:55-6:25/km and surges around controlled 5k effort. Cool down 3-5 min easy.
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Keep the whole run continuous. Surges should feel quick but relaxed, and the easy jog should be active enough that breathing stays honest without ruining the next rep. Because the run base is still low, finish feeling like you could complete one more surge with good mechanics.

exerciseTemplates.notes: Phase 2 Tuesday: 5k-focused Fartlek work, RPE 7-8, using repeatable surges near current 5k pace with active easy jog recovery. Rough surge pace guide: 5:08-5:15/km, with easy jog segments relaxed but still moving. Sits 72 h before Friday squats.
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Keep the run continuous and the reps repeatable. Surge pace should look like controlled 5k running, not a race finish. Easy jog pace stays easy enough to restore posture and breathing, but never turns into standing rest. Stop before the session turns into a leg-destroying workout that bleeds into Friday.

exerciseTemplates.notes: Easy long run for aerobic durability, RPE 5-6. Rough pace guide: 6:45-7:25/km. Keep it relaxed enough that you could breathe through your nose for most of the run.
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: This is not a workout. Stay tall, keep cadence light, and protect the knee by shortening the stride before the pace creeps up. Walk 30-60 seconds if needed rather than forcing continuous running when the base is still low.

Forearms shoulder-width, elbows under shoulders. Squeeze glutes, posterior pelvic tilt, ribs down. Body forms one line from heel to crown — no hip sag, no butt in the air. If the lower back arches, end the set early.

exerciseTemplates.notes: 10/side - anti-rotation hold each rep
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Stand side-on to the band, hands at the sternum. Press the hands straight out and resist the band's rotational pull — the trunk should not move at all. 1 s hold at full extension, return slowly. Anti-rotation is the goal; if the torso twists, lighten the band.

exerciseTemplates.notes: Slow eccentric. Knee/hamstring support.
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Lie on your back, heels on the rower seat, hips lifted into a glute bridge. Pull the seat toward the hips by curling the heels under, keeping the hips high the entire time. 3 s eccentric. If hamstrings cramp, shorten the ROM rather than dropping the hips.

exerciseTemplates.notes: Anchor upper back, grip bench edge behind head. Stop rule: lower back arches or ribs flare = rep done. Never train to failure.
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Lie on a bench, grip the edge above your head. Lift the legs and hips so the body forms a vertical line from shoulders to feet, knees tucked tight to the chest. Lower under control, keeping the lower back glued to neutral. Stop the rep — and the set — if the lumbar arches or ribs flare.

exerciseTemplates.notes: If 6 s is clean, add 1 slow negative.
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Same vertical start position as the tuck variant, but extend one leg fully while the other stays tucked. Hold rigid; the extended leg adds a long lever the trunk must resist. If a clean 6 s hold is easy, finish with one slow negative rather than chasing more time.

exerciseTemplates.notes: 5-count eccentric, tuck back to start. Stop well before shaking.
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Kick or assist into the top vertical position. Lower the entire body — straight as a board — over a 5 s count, fighting the lumbar arch the whole way. Tuck the knees once the heels are ~30 cm off the bench to reset. Stop well before the trunk starts shaking.

exerciseTemplates.notes: External rotation at top of pull
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Band at face height, wide overhand grip. Pull the band toward the eyebrows while flaring the elbows wide and externally rotating so the hands finish above the elbows. Pause 1 s at the top. The cue is "show me your biceps," not "row to your chin."

exerciseTemplates.notes: Vertical press stays light and clean. +10-15 kg Wks 1-8, +5-10 kg Wk 9. Full reach, ribs down, smooth arc. Skip if symptoms elevated.
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Half-kneeling with the down-leg matching the pressing arm. Bar starts at the shoulder, ribs stacked over hips. Press up and slightly forward in a smooth arc, fully extending the elbow without shrugging. Lower under control. If shoulder symptoms flare, skip — vertical pressing is dispensable.

exerciseTemplates.notes: Slow - ankle/knee stability, goose-foot management. Part of Thursday B-circuit (run with Face Pulls / Landmine Press / Banded ER / Side Plank as one integrated 5-exercise circuit, 2 rounds).
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Stand on one foot on a small step, other foot tucked behind. Rise onto the ball of the foot fully (1 s pause at the top), then descend under control past flat for a heel drop. Use a wall or post for balance only — load the working calf, don't hop.

exerciseTemplates.notes: Lateral trunk stability. Part of Thursday B-circuit.
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Forearm under shoulder, body rigid in one line. Stack feet (or stagger if needed for balance) and lift the hips so the bottom side does not sag. Squeeze glutes and obliques. End the set when the hips drop, not when the time runs out.

exerciseTemplates.notes: Light - rotator cuff endurance. Part of Thursday B-circuit.
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Elbow tucked at the side, 90° bend. Anchor the band so it pulls across the body. Rotate the forearm out without letting the elbow drift away from the ribs. Slow and deliberate — this is rotator cuff endurance, not a strength move.

exerciseTemplates.notes: Thursday Ring Push-Up Continuation Rule. Controlled horizontal-push skill only; stop well before fatigue.
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Set the rings high enough that every rep stays crisp. Hold a hollow-body plank, let the wrists rotate naturally, keep elbows 30-45° from the torso, lower for 2 s, pause for 1 s, then press smoothly. Stop when the rings wobble, depth shortens, or elbows flare.

exerciseTemplates.notes: Tuesday Day Template slot E. Real elbow-rehab exposure (not just MWF warm-up). Non-negotiable in Phase 2; reduce to 2x15 in Phase 3 (deload + realization).
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Forearm supported on the bench, palm down, holding a 1-2 kg DB. Use the other hand to lift the weight to full wrist extension, then slowly lower over 3 s using only the working forearm. Tyler-twist style eccentric. This is the standalone elbow exposure for the week — make sure all 3 sets are completed cleanly.

exerciseTemplates.notes: Tuck only - no German hang yet. Stop any sharp impingement.
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Hang from rings with a tight tuck (knees to chest). Pull the knees up and through the rings, rolling backwards until the hips reach ring height — stop there, then reverse the motion under control. Do not chase a German hang yet. Any sharp shoulder pinch ends the set.

exerciseTemplates.notes: Hold 2 s in partial German hang.
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: From a tucked inversion, slowly extend through the back of the rings to a partial German hang (arms straight, hips below shoulders, but stopping above full extension). Hold 2 s, then reverse. Build slowly — full ROM unlocks only when shoulders feel calm at this depth.

exerciseTemplates.notes: Full Skin-the-Cat with full German hang.
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Full Skin-the-Cat: from inversion, extend all the way through to a complete German hang with arms straight, body extended, toes pointed. Pause briefly at the bottom, then reverse to inverted. Move continuously and smoothly — never drop or jerk through the bottom.

exerciseTemplates.notes: Slow descent, perfect knee tracking. Unilateral stability slot.
exerciseTemplates.coachingNotes: Box height roughly knee-level. Place the working foot fully on the box, drive through the heel — no push-off from the back leg. Stand tall at the top, then lower under control over 3 s. Both DBs hang at the sides; use straps if grip is the limiter.

phases.name: Phase 1: Accumulation and Athletic Base
phases.description: Rebuild tolerance around a stable hybrid week: Tuesday establishes repeatable Fartlek rhythm, Thursday stays easy, and the barbell days accumulate clean, bench, and squat volume without accessory drift.

days.name: Monday — Bench + Pulling
days.description: Bench heavy working set of 6 at 62.5 kg, then backoffs

exercises.notes: Heavy working set at 62.5 kg for 6 reps. Stop if bar speed drops.
2 backoff set(s) at 57.5 kg. Crisp volume only.
Moderate vertical pull. Stay smooth and stop before elbow irritation rises.
Balancing row slot. Keep scapular control perfect.

days.name: Tuesday — GPP, Trunk, Hamstrings, Rehab
days.description: Introductory Fartlek + simple trunk and tendon work

exercises.notes: Week 1: 6 x 1 min surge / 1 min easy jog. Keep surges around controlled 5k effort and easy jog recoveries active enough that the run stays continuous.

days.name: Wednesday — Power Clean Quality
days.description: Power emphasis and clean positions

exercises.notes: Power primer. Full reset between reps; stop if height or distance drops.
exercises.coachingNotes: Start tall, use a quick counter movement, and project forward with a violent arm swing. Stick the landing softly and reset every rep.

exercises.notes: 60 kg for crisp doubles. Reset every rep and treat the set like EMOM work.

days.name: Thursday — Restoration + Structural Balance
days.description: Easy recovery run + structural support

exercises.notes: Week 1: 12 min easy run at conversational pace, then 4 x 15 s relaxed strides with full walk-back recovery.

days.name: Friday — Squat Strength + Secondary Squat
days.description: Lower strength accumulation + squat backoff

exercises.notes: Power primer. Full reset between reps; stop if height or distance drops.
exercises.coachingNotes: Start tall, use a quick counter movement, and project forward with a violent arm swing. Stick the landing softly and reset every rep.
